entries.label_en: Note: The NHIA describes case classification for Western-medicine outpatient fees as follows: (1) For daily-dose drug-fee billing, the class is '01: Western-medicine general case', but chronic disease may not be billed as a general case. (2) For NHIA-announced chronic diseases, the class should be '04: Western-medicine chronic disease'. (3) When a physician confirms the insured's condition is stable and the same prescription can be used long-term, a 'refillable prescription' may be issued and the class for that visit is '04: chronic disease'; if the insured presents the refillable chronic prescription directly for dispensing, the class is '08: chronic refillable-prescription dispensing'. (4) Cases not covered above are '09: Western-medicine other special case'. (5) When acute and chronic disease are treated together, the class is '09: other special case'; if a refillable chronic prescription is also issued, report class '04: chronic disease' and fill item 22 'days of medication' with the highest day count among that visit's chronic drugs (revised ROC 93/03). (6) A '01: general case' that is dispensed via referral should be reported as '09: Western-medicine other special case'.

entries.label_en: Note: The NHIA describes case classification for Western-medicine outpatient fees as follows: (1) For daily-dose drug-fee billing, the class is '01: Western-medicine general case', but chronic disease may not be billed as a general case. (2) For NHIA-announced chronic diseases, the class should be '04: Western-medicine chronic disease'. (3) When a physician confirms the condition is stable and the same prescription can be used long-term, a 'refillable prescription' may be issued and that visit's class is '04: chronic disease'; if the insured presents the refillable prescription directly, the class is '08: chronic refillable-prescription dispensing'. (4) Cases not covered above are '09: Western-medicine other special case'. (5) When acute and chronic disease are treated together, the class is '09'; if a refillable chronic prescription is also issued, report class '04', and fill item 22 'days of medication' with the highest day count among the chronic drugs (revised ROC 93/03). (6) A '01: general case' dispensed via referral should be reported as '09'.
